rows.statement: MCL sprain, NCAA football: grade I about 10 days, grade II about 35 days missed; every grade I and II player returned; managed non-operatively in nearly all cases.

sources.citation: Motamedi AR et al, J Am Acad Orthop Surg Glob Res Rev 2017;1(5):e019, doi:10.5435/JAAOSGlobal-D-17-00019 (NCAA Division I football, one institution 2001-2007, 47 MCL injuries)
sources.locator: "Grade I injuries resulted in an average of 10 days of missed training time"; "grade II injuries resulted in an average of 35 days of missed practice time"; grade I and II all returned; 98% of MCL injuries grade I or II; nearly all non-operative
sources.quote: grade II injuries resulted in an average of 35 days of missed practice time

rows.notes: College population, one institution.

sources.citation: Bodendorfer BM et al, Arthrosc Sports Med Rehabil 2021;3(4):e1097, doi:10.1016/j.asmr.2021.03.015 (NFL 1998-2020, 258 pectoralis major injuries)
sources.locator: "85.3% players (220 of 258) returned to competition following PM injury, with a mean time to RTP of 165.8 +/- 147.9 days (range 2-668 days)"

sources.citation: Wise PM et al, Orthop J Sports Med 2021;9(6), doi:10.1177/23259671211018707 (NFL 2010-2018, 63 ruptures)
sources.locator: "A total of 85.7% of players returned to play in the NFL after injury."

rows.notes: Return rates agree (85.3 vs 85.7). Time figures from the first study only.

sources.locator: Table 5 metacarpal fracture time loss 12.3 +/- 25.8 days, median 2.5 (0-148); 71.4% of all hand and wrist injuries no time loss; 7.4% surgery

rows.statement: Cramp: removes a player for a few plays to a series; per-play probability rises with heat index above 85 F, snap load, body mass and low conditioning, falls with rotation and hydration. Rates are design values.

sources.citation: Bible D11.7.1 (project design); heat cramps 43% of NCAA football heat illness cases 2009-2015 (J Athl Train 2019), about 70% in one southeastern season (PubMed 17043703)
sources.locator: D11.7.1 football facts

rows.notes: Existence of cramps as most common heat illness is sourced (2 of 3 per bible); all rates are an assumption. No NFL in-game rate found.

rows.statement: Heat illness: rare, removes the player for the day; illness spread: entry 3 percent per team-week, 15 percent per exposed player in a room, absence 1 to 3 days.
